title: Lecture 3 · Storage and retrieval
outline: STATUS: DONE for the architect brief: helpers common.js to common-4.js written, asserted on load, eslint and prettier clean, and exercised in a throwaway stills render (recs, entries, panel, ptr, span, disk, ram, mergeRig, tree all draw; the scratch page is deleted); page videos/ds-3.html, audio stub and all placeholder scenes load with no page errors, total 122.5 s; title card checked (fits at 92 px). LEFT: the recap and scenes 2-10 are placeholders; the specs give layouts as a starting point, so scene authors should adjust coordinates after a stills render (the throwaway test only checked that each helper draws, not the exact spec layouts). VIDEO ds-3 (Data Science COM3021, lecture 3 'Storage and retrieval'), 11 scenes, about 122.5 s: title (4), two jobs / two workloads (10), the log: set, get, delete (13), the cost: append 1 step vs scan n steps (11), hash index (12), segments and compaction (13), limits of the hash index (10.5), merging sorted segments (14), sparse index (11.5), memtable write and read path (14.5), recap (9). STORY: a database stores and retrieves; the design follows the workload (2). The simplest store is a log: set appends, get scans for the LAST line of the key, delete appends a tombstone (3). Appending costs 1 step, reading n lines costs n steps (O(n)), so we need an index (4). A hash index keeps key -> byte offset in memory: one jump per get, every append moves the pointer (5). Segments cap the file size and compaction keeps the latest value per key (6). The hash index needs all keys in RAM and cannot do ranges (7). SSTables: segments sorted by key, each key once, merged like merge sort with the newest copy winning and tombstones deleting (8); sorted order lets the index be sparse (jump near, scan a short block) and ranges work (9); a memtable (sorted tree in memory) absorbs writes and is flushed as a new SSTable; reads go memtable, newest segment, older ones, first hit wins (10). Not covered (lessons 3.1-3.3 and workshop 3.W): binary formats, crash recovery and partial writes, concurrency control, the hash-map rebuild after a restart, compression of blocks, the write-ahead log of the workshop; the recap points to Workshop 3.W (ds-engine). Lessons: ds-log 3.1, ds-hashidx 3.2, ds-sstable 3.3 (js/content/ds/ds-l23-02.js to -05.js), boss ds3-boss (Pedalo bike-rental telemetry, boss-ds-23.js), workshop ds-engine 3.W (ds-workshops-03.js). COLOURS (whole video): grey = data on disk (records, log lines, segment files, neutral labels); blue = the request (the key we ask for, the scan pointer, a head ring, the record being read); green = good (found, newest, kept, written, the merged result, a tick); red = dead or bad (a tombstone, an overwritten old copy that is dropped, a miss, 'does not fit'); orange = addresses and costs (byte offsets, step counters, attention); purple = in memory (hash map, sparse index, memtable). All text 28 px or more; symbols are SVG (L5.tick / L5.cross / L5.arrow, a tombstone is the red cross inside the record badge). Pass everything to every draw call every frame (pure). SHARED CONVENTIONS. Examples: bike-share keys (bike, dock) for the log, cat-video play counts (mew, purr, yawn) for the index and segments, kitty1..kitty6 for the range limit, fruit keys (apple, fig, kiwi, mango, plum, grape, date) for the merge and the memtable, words hand..harbour for the sparse index; scene 10 starts from the merged segment of scene 8. A record is a sticker 'key [value]' (D3.recs); a tombstone shows a red cross in the value badge. Disk things are grey, memory things purple; byte offsets are orange mono numbers in a gutter. Every number comes from D3 (common.js), asserted on page load.

title: A database stores data
and finds it again
caps: Some work is many small writes.
Other work is one big read.
Design follows the workload.
scenes.spec:
Helpers: const V = window.VID, D3 = V.d3, L5 = V.l5; const {ramp, flash, clamp, lerp, ease: E} = V. IDEA: a database has two jobs, store data and give it back; the right design depends on the workload: transactional (many small writes: orders, payments) or analytics (big reads over lots of data: reports). Data: D3.LOAD = {txn: {writes: 9}, ana: {cols: 4, rows: 6, cells: 24, answer: 1}}.

LAYOUT (two halves). LEFT: D3.tag(stage, {x: 80, y: 8, text: 'transactional', tone: 'grey'}); D3.disk at centre (300, 300) size 130 in an L5.svg layer (grey); nine packets = D3.chip(stage, {w: 84, h: 52, text: 'set', fs: 28, tone: 'blue', radius: 16}) travelling along y 274 from x 20 to the disk's left edge (x 235); D3.stat(stage, {x: 40, y: 470, w: 270, h: 80, label: 'writes', tone: 'orange'}) counting 0 to 9. RIGHT: D3.tag {x: 640, y: 8, text: 'analytics'}; the table = D3.recs(stage, {x: 530, y: 120, w: 84, h: 40, gap: 8, colGap: 8, cols: 4, recs: 24 x {}, radius: 12}) (360 x 280, empty grey tiles); D3.stat {x: 530, y: 440, w: 360, h: 80, label: 'rows read', tone: 'orange'}; D3.tag {x: 600, y: 540, text: '1 answer', tone: 'green', solid: true}.

TIMELINE. 0.3-0.8 left tag and disk pop. 0.9-4.3 the nine packets fly in 0.3 s apart (each 0.7 s along its lane, shrinking to scale 0.3 and fading as it enters the disk; the disk bumps 1.06 on every arrival with flash) while the 'writes' stat counts up on each arrival (bump). 4.7-5.2 right tag and table pop (tiles in row order, 0.03 s apart). 5.4-7.6 a scan band: row r (4 tiles) turns blue for 0.3 s from 5.4 + 0.35 r and stays blue-tinted afterwards (tone 'blue'); the 'rows read' stat counts 4, 8, ... 24 with it. 7.8-8.3 the table turns green-tinted and the '1 answer' tag pops. 8.0-9.8 hold; both halves stay on screen, calm final frame.

title: The simplest database
is a file you append to
caps: A log is a file you only add to.
Set adds a line at the end.
Get scans for the last line of a key.
Delete adds a tombstone line.
The newest line says: deleted.
scenes.spec:
Helpers: const V = window.VID, D3 = V.d3, L5 = V.l5; const {ramp, flash, clamp, lerp, ease: E} = V. IDEA: the simplest key-value database is a log file: set appends 'key value' at the end (old lines stay), get scans for the LAST line of that key, delete appends a TOMBSTONE (a delete marker), nothing is erased. Data: D3.LOG (bike-share): lines [bike 1, dock 2, bike 3, dock TOMB]; D3.LOG.getBike = {scanned 3, hits [0, 2], win 2, value 3}; D3.LOG.getDock = {scanned 4, hits [1, 3], win 3, deleted: true}. Assert with D3.same when the scene is built.

LAYOUT. Panel D3.panel(stage, {x: 290, y: 10, w: 380, h: 420, title: 'log file', tone: 'grey'}). Lines = D3.recs(stage, {x: 330, y: 80, w: 300, h: 56, gap: 12, cols: 1, recs: D3.LOG.lines}) (4 rows, y 80 to 332). Command tags on the left: D3.tag(stage, {x: 20, y: rowY - 29, text: 'set bike 1', tone: 'blue'}) for each op (texts from D3.LOG.steps: 'set bike 1', 'set dock 2', 'set bike 3', 'get bike', 'delete dock', 'get dock'), each pops at x 20 and slides right to the line it creates. Result tags on the right (x 700): D3.tag {y: 150, text: 'bike = 3', tone: 'green', solid: true} and D3.tag {y: 290, text: 'dock: deleted', tone: 'red', solid: true}. A small tag D3.tag {text: 'tombstone', tone: 'red'} next to line 3 (x 690, y 308).

TIMELINE. 0.3-0.9 panel and empty log pop. SET: 1.2-1.8 'set bike 1' pops, slides in, line 0 pops (f.set(0, {k})); 2.2-2.8 line 1; 3.0-3.6 line 2 (each tag fades once its line is in). GET bike: 5.4 'get bike' tag pops; 5.6-6.6 a blue ring walks down lines 0, 1, 2 (0.35 s each; ring each in turn, lines 0 and 2 turn blue because their key is bike); 6.8 line 2 turns green solid, line 0 stays blue-tinted; 7.0-7.6 'bike = 3' pops. DELETE: 8.4 'delete dock' pops; 8.8-9.5 line 3 appears as a red tombstone (rec has tomb: true, red tone) and the 'tombstone' tag pops. GET dock: 10.2 'get dock'; 10.4-11.5 ring walks lines 0-3 (lines 1 and 3 blue); 11.6 line 3 turns red solid; 11.8-12.3 'dock: deleted' pops. Hold.

title: Appending is cheap,
finding means scanning
caps: A write is one append: one step.
A read scans every line.
Twice the data, twice the scan.
We need an index.
scenes.spec:
Helpers: const V = window.VID, D3 = V.d3, L5 = V.l5; const {ramp, flash, clamp, lerp, ease: E} = V. IDEA: a write is one append (1 step); a read scans every line (n lines, n steps: O(n)) because the last line for the key may be the very last; twice the data means twice the scan, so a log needs an index. Data: D3.COST = {write: 1, first: {n: 8, scan: 8}, second: {n: 16, scan: 16}, ratio: 2}.

LAYOUT. The log as tiles: D3.recs(stage, {x: 30, y: 150, w: 96, h: 70, gap: 12, colGap: 12, cols: 8, recs: 16 x {}, radius: 18}) (two rows of 8, tile i at x 30 + 108 (i % 8), y 150 + 82 (i div 8)); only tiles 0-7 are shown at first (7 old lines plus the newly appended one). Stats D3.stat(stage, {x: 30, y: 8, w: 300, h: 80, label: 'write', tone: 'green'}) reading '1 step', and D3.stat {x: 360, y: 8, w: 400, h: 80, label: 'read', tone: 'orange'} counting steps. D3.tag(stage, {x: 30, y: 400, text: 'O(n)', tone: 'orange', solid: true}) and D3.tag {x: 200, y: 400, text: 'n lines = n steps', tone: 'orange'} (appear late). Under the second row (y 340 to 400) space stays free for the tags.

TIMELINE. 0.3-1.0 tiles 0-6 pop (0.05 s apart). WRITE: 1.2-1.8 a blue packet chip (D3.chip w 84 h 52 text 'set') flies to tile 7, tile 7 pops green; the 'write' stat pops reading '1 step' (2.0). READ: 3.4 the 'read' stat pops reading 0; 3.6-5.6 a blue ring runs over tiles 0-7 (0.25 s each) and the stat counts 1..8; tile 7 turns green solid at the end. DOUBLE: 6.4-7.0 tiles 8-15 pop (second row); 7.2-9.0 the ring runs over all 16 tiles (0.11 s each, faster) while the stat counts 1..16; 9.1 tags 'O(n)' and 'n lines = n steps' pop. Hold. Numbers: the stat must show D3.COST.first.scan then D3.COST.second.scan.

title: A map in memory
jumps straight to a key
caps: Keep a map in memory: key to byte offset.
Get mew: look up its offset.
One jump, one disk read.
A new write moves the pointer.
scenes.spec:
Helpers: const V = window.VID, D3 = V.d3, L5 = V.l5; const {ramp, flash, clamp, lerp, ease: E} = V. IDEA: keep a hash map IN MEMORY from every key to the byte offset of its latest line in the log; a get looks the key up and jumps to that offset (one disk read instead of scanning); every append updates the map. Data (cat-video play counts, lesson 3.2): D3.HASH = {recs: the first nine lines of D3.PLAYS [mew 1, mew 2, purr 1, yawn 1, mew 3, purr 2, mew 4, yawn 2, mew 5], offs [0, 6, 12, 19, 26, 32, 39, 45, 52], map {mew: 52, purr: 32, yawn: 45}, get {k: mew, off 52, value 5, reads 1, scan 9}, write {rec: purr 3, off 58, mapAfter: purr 58}, get2 {purr, off 58, value 3}}.

LAYOUT. LEFT disk side: D3.tag(stage, {x: 30, y: 4, text: 'on disk', tone: 'grey'}); the file D3.recs(stage, {x: 30, y: 74, w: 220, h: 48, gap: 6, cols: 1, gutter: 80, recs: D3.HASH.recs + the new purr 3 as the 10th line (ten rows, y 74 to 584), marks: offsets as strings, markTone orange}) (row i at y 74 + 54 i; the gutter shows 0, 6, 12, 19, 26, 32, 39, 45, 52, 58). RIGHT memory side: D3.tag {x: 560, y: 4, text: 'in memory', tone: 'purple'}; D3.entries(stage, {x: 540, y: 80, rows: [{key: 'mew', val: 52}, {key: 'purr', val: 32}, {key: 'yawn', val: 45}], keyW: 130, valW: 96, h: 56, gap: 14}) with a D3.panel behind it (x 520, y 70, w 300, h 250, tone 'purple'). Pointers: three D3.ptr (orange) from each entry's valRight(i) to the gutter of its line (row 8 for mew, 5 purr, 7 yawn): use f.gutterMid(i) offset a little right; one extra ptr for the jump. Stat D3.stat {x: 540, y: 400, w: 330, h: 80, label: 'disk reads', tone: 'orange'}. Result tag D3.tag {x: 620, y: 510, text: 'mew = 5', tone: 'green', solid: true}.

TIMELINE. 0.3-1.4 file lines 0-8 pop (0.06 s apart); line 9 (purr 3) stays hidden until 8.8. 1.5-2.4 memory tag, panel and entries pop. 2.5-3.8 the three pointers draw on and the lines they point at turn blue-tinted (latest line of each key). 4.6 get: entry 'mew' rings blue; 5.0-5.6 a blue D3.ptr jumps from the entry to line 8 (gutter 52), line 8 turns green solid; 5.8 'mew = 5' pops and the stat reads 1 (bump). 7.0 stat label stays; 7.2-7.9 a grey note is not needed. WRITE: 8.6-9.4 line 9 pops in green (purr 3, gutter 58); 9.4-10.2 the purr entry's number changes 32 -> 58 (e.set(1, {val: '58', bump})) and its pointer slides from line 5 to line 9 (ptr.set with moving x2, y2). 10.4-11.6 get purr: ring, jump to line 9, tag 'purr = 3'. Hold.

title: Cut the log into segments,
then compact them
caps: A log that only grows fills the disk.
So close a file at its size limit.
Many records, only three keys.
Compaction keeps the latest value per key.
scenes.spec:
Helpers: const V = window.VID, D3 = V.d3, L5 = V.l5; const {ramp, flash, clamp, lerp, ease: E} = V. IDEA: the log is cut into segments (a file is closed when it reaches a size limit and the next write opens a new one); compaction then keeps only the LATEST value per key and drops older copies. Data: D3.SEG = {limit: 6, segs: [[mew 1, mew 2, purr 1, yawn 1, mew 3, purr 2], [mew 4, yawn 2, mew 5, purr 3, mew 6, purr 4]], before 12, after 3, keep [7, 10, 11] (flat indices), drop [0..6, 8, 9], out [yawn 2, mew 6, purr 4], next: 2}.

LAYOUT. Three panels side by side (D3.panel, y 40, w 280, h 230, plain): segment 1 at x 14, segment 2 at x 328, segment 3 at x 642; each with its records D3.recs(stage, {x: panelX + 14, y: 100, w: 120, h: 52, gap: 8, colGap: 10, cols: 2, recs: D3.SEG.segs[s]}) (2 x 3 block; w 120 fits 'mew 1', 'purr 4' at fs 28 only if fs 26 is avoided: use w 126). Segment 3 is a dashed (tone grey, plain false) empty panel until 6.0. Tags under the panels: D3.tag(stage, {y: 290}) with 'closed', 'closed', 'active' (grey / grey / green). Compaction row (y 340 to 600): the compacted segment D3.panel {x: 14 + 134?, y: 360, w: 280, h: 200, tone: 'green', title: 'compacted'} with D3.recs {recs: D3.SEG.out, w: 126, cols: 2}; stat D3.stat {x: 600, y: 360, w: 330, h: 80, label: 'records', tone: 'orange'} counting 12 -> 3.

TIMELINE. 0.3-0.8 panel 1 pops. 0.9-2.3 its six records pop (0.2 s apart) and the stat reads 6. 3.0-3.4 panel 1 gets its 'closed' tag; 3.5-4.9 panel 2 and its six records fill (0.22 s apart, stat 12); 5.0-5.5 'closed' tag; 5.8-6.2 the empty segment-3 panel opens with 'active'. COMPACT: 6.6-7.8 the records that are NOT kept (D3.SEG.drop) turn red one after another (0.12 s apart, tone 'red', ghost on the dropped ones from 7.8) while the three kept ones (flat indices 7, 10, 11) turn green solid; 8.0 caption moment; 9.6-11.0 copies of the three survivors slide down into the compacted panel (positions from recs.mid) and the stat counts 12 -> 3; 11.0-12.6 panels 1 and 2 fade to ghosts (o 0.5 is allowed only on the whole panel, not text: use ghost tone). Hold the compacted panel in green.

title: Keys must fit in memory,
and ranges are slow
caps: The whole map must fit in memory.
A range needs one lookup per key.
Sorted keys sit side by side.
scenes.spec:
Helpers: const V = window.VID, D3 = V.d3, L5 = V.l5; const {ramp, flash, clamp, lerp, ease: E} = V. IDEA: two limits of the hash index. (1) The map lives in RAM, so it works only while ALL keys fit; (2) a hash map has no key order, so a range query (kitty2 to kitty5) needs a separate lookup for every key, whereas sorted keys sit side by side (the teaser for the next scene). Data: D3.LIM.ram = {slots 6, keys 12, fit 6, over 6}; D3.LIM.range = {keys kitty1..kitty6, from kitty2, to kitty5, want [kitty2..kitty5], lookups 4, table [null, kitty3, kitty6, kitty1, kitty4, null, kitty2, kitty5] (FNV-1a mod 8), wantBuckets [6, 1, 4, 7], sorted, wantAt [1, 2, 3, 4]}.

PART A (0.3-4.9): D3.ram(x 468, y 250, size 150, 'purple') in an L5.svg layer? No: a purple D3.panel(stage, {x: 250, y: 90, w: 436, h: 230, tone: 'purple', title: 'memory'}) holding six dashed slots = D3.recs(stage, {x: 270, y: 150, w: 120, h: 52, gap: 10, colGap: 12, cols: 3, recs: 6 x {text: ''}, tone: 'purple'}) (all ghost). Twelve key chips D3.chip(stage, {w: 120, h: 52, text: 'key', fs: 28, tone: 'blue', radius: 16}) fly in from the right edge (x 936) one every 0.25 s from 0.8: the first six land in the slots (they turn solid purple), the next six cannot enter: they stop at the panel's right wall and pile up outside in two columns at x 720 to 900, y 150 to 360 and turn red. D3.tag {x: 330, y: 340, text: 'does not fit', tone: 'red', solid: true} pops at 3.6. Stat D3.stat {x: 250, y: 410, w: 436, h: 80, label: 'keys / slots', tone: 'orange'} reading 12 / 6.
PART B (5.0-10.3): Part A fades out 4.7-5.1. The hash table = D3.recs(stage, {x: 138, y: 70, w: 150, h: 52, gap: 12, colGap: 12, cols: 4, recs: D3.LIM.range.table (null -> {} empty ghost slots)}) two rows of four (buckets 0-3 on top, 4-7 below), keys pop at 5.1; D3.tag {x: 330, y: 8, text: 'kitty2 to kitty5', tone: 'blue'}; the four wanted keys light blue one by one (5.7, 6.3, 6.9, 7.5; buckets 6, 1, 4, 7) each with a blue ptr jumping to a small orange counter D3.stat {x: 338, y: 260, w: 260, h: 80, label: 'lookups', tone: 'orange'} counting 1..4. At 8.4 the sorted strip D3.recs {x: 30, y: 420, w: 130, h: 52, gap: 8, colGap: 8, cols: 6, recs: sorted keys} pops; D3.span (green) under chips wantAt 1..4 (x1 = left of chip 1, x2 = right of chip 4, y 490) draws on 8.8-9.6 and chips 1-4 turn green. Hold.

title: Sorted segments merge
like merge sort
caps: Three sorted segments, oldest left.
Take the smallest key first.
Repeats: the newest wins.
A newer tombstone deletes it.
One sorted segment, no old values.
scenes.spec:
Helpers: const V = window.VID, D3 = V.d3, L5 = V.l5; const {ramp, flash, clamp, lerp, ease: E} = V. IDEA: an SSTable is a segment sorted by key with each key once; several are merged exactly like the merge step of merge sort: pointers sit at the smallest unread key of each segment, the smallest key goes out, and when several segments hold it the NEWEST copy wins; a tombstone as winner means the key is written nowhere. Data: D3.MERGE = {segs [[apple 1, fig 2, mango 3, plum 4], [apple 5, kiwi 6, mango 7], [fig 8, kiwi TOMB, plum 9]], frames (5): apple (seg 2 wins 5), fig (seg 3 wins 8), kiwi (the newest is the tombstone: nothing written), mango (seg 2 wins 7), plum (seg 3 wins 9); out [apple 5, fig 8, mango 7, plum 9]; 10 records in, 4 out}.

ONE FIGURE: const m = D3.mergeRig(stage, {x: 35, y: 10, colW: 200, gap: 22, rowH: 52, rowGap: 10}) (866 px wide; segment columns at x 35, 257, 479 and merged at 701; chips from y 72 to 310; age arrow 'older -> newer' at y 354). Use w 200 chips: 'apple 5' fits. Add a blue pill D3.tag(stage, {x: 330, y: 440, text: 'smallest key: apple', tone: 'blue'}) (text from m.info(p).frame.key, centred under the rig) and a red D3.tag {x: 330, y: 520, text: 'tombstone: delete', tone: 'red', solid: true} shown only during step 2 (p 2.5-3).

TIMELINE (p = progress, drive m.update({p, k})). 0.3-2.3 k 0 -> 1 (headings, segments, merged heading pop). Steps: p = 0 until 2.8; then p advances so step 0 (apple) spans 2.8-4.4, step 1 (fig) 4.4-6.0, step 2 (kiwi, tombstone) 6.0-7.9, step 3 (mango) 7.9-9.4, step 4 (plum) 9.4-10.9: use a piecewise-linear p(t) through those times, ending p = 5 at 10.9. The smallest-key pill follows m.info(p).frame.key (pop on every new step, hidden when done). 11.1-14.0 hold the final picture: the four green merged records, the used source records as ghosts; caption 'One sorted segment, no old values.' Merged output must equal D3.MERGE.out (assert).

title: Sorted keys need only
a sparse index
caps: A segment sorted by key.
The index holds only some keys.
Jump to the key before it.
Scan a short block.
A range: one jump, read on.
scenes.spec:
Helpers: const V = window.VID, D3 = V.d3, L5 = V.l5; const {ramp, flash, clamp, lerp, ease: E} = V. IDEA: because the segment is sorted, the in-memory index needs only SOME keys (the first of each block): to find a key, jump to the nearest indexed key before it and scan one short block; sorted keys also make a range one jump plus reading on. Data: D3.SPARSE = {recs: 12 sorted keys hand, handbag, handful, handle, handsome, handy, hang, hangar, hanger, happen, happy, harbour (value = record number), block 4, offs, index [{hand, i 0, off 0}, {handsome, i 4, off 36}, {hanger, i 8, off 71}], find {key handbag, via hand, reads [0, 1], hit 1}, range {from handbag, to handy, via hand, hits [1..5], scanned [0..6], jumps 1}}.

LAYOUT. The segment = D3.recs(stage, {x: 40, y: 250, w: 270, h: 52, gap: 8, colGap: 28, rows: 4, recs: D3.SPARSE.recs minus values (key only: map to {k})}) three block columns at x 40, 338, 636, chips y 250 to 458 (use w 250). Behind each column a grey D3.panel (x col - 12, y 232, h 240, w 274, plain). The index = D3.entries(stage, {x: ..., y: 20, rows: D3.SPARSE.index.map(e => ({key: e.key, val: e.off})), keyW: 150?, valW: 80}) laid out as THREE separate one-row entries above their blocks (D3.entries called three times at x 60, 358, 656, y 100) in purple with a purple tag D3.tag {x: 330, y: 8, text: 'index in memory', tone: 'purple'}; a D3.ptr (orange) from each entry down to its block's first chip. Query tag D3.tag(stage, {x: 40, y: 540, text: 'get handbag', tone: 'blue'}); stat D3.stat {x: 560, y: 520, w: 330, h: 80, label: 'records read', tone: 'orange'}.

TIMELINE. 0.3-2.4 chips pop column by column (0.08 s apart). 3.0-4.6 the three index entries pop with their pointers drawing on; the tag 'index in memory' pops; a small orange tag shows '3 of 12 keys'. 5.6 'get handbag' pops; 5.8 the entry 'hand' rings blue (the largest key <= handbag; handsome is too big); 6.1-6.7 a blue ptr jumps to block 1 (chip 0). 7.6-8.6 the ring walks chip 0 (hand, no) then chip 1 (handbag, green solid); stat counts 1, 2. 9.3-11.1 RANGE: tag text changes to 'handbag to handy' (swap text), D3.span green over chips 1..5 draws on from left to right (it crosses into block 2) and chips 1..5 turn green one by one (0.25 s apart). Hold.

title: Writes land in memory,
then reach disk sorted
caps: Writes land in memory first.
A tree keeps the keys in order.
When full, write it out in order.
New writes get a new memtable.
Reads check memory, then newest.
First hit wins: fig 11, not 8.
scenes.spec:
Helpers: const V = window.VID, D3 = V.d3, L5 = V.l5; const {ramp, flash, clamp, lerp, ease: E} = V. IDEA: the write path and the read path of an SSTable store. Writes arrive in random order and go into the MEMTABLE (a balanced tree in memory that keeps keys sorted); when it is full, walk the tree in order and write it to disk as a new SSTable (the newest segment) while new writes go to a fresh memtable. A read checks the memtable, then the newest segment, then older ones, and stops at the first hit (newest wins). Data: D3.MEM = {old: [apple 5, fig 8, mango 7, plum 9] (the segment from scene 8), limit 5, writes [kiwi 10, fig 11, plum 12, apple 13, grape 14], nodes (tree: kiwi root, fig left, plum right, apple left of fig, grape right of fig; nodes sit left to right in sorted order), walk [3, 1, 4, 0, 2], flushed [apple 13, fig 11, grape 14, kiwi 10, plum 12], next {date 15}, getFig {checks 2, value 11}, getMango {checks 3, value 7}}.

LAYOUT. Memory zone: D3.panel(stage, {x: 40, y: 0, w: 856, h: 290, tone: 'purple', plain: false, title: 'memory: memtable'}); tree = D3.tree(stage, {x: 50, y: 56, nodeW: 156, nodeH: 52, gap: 12, levelH: 84}) (width 5 x 156 + 4 x 12 = 828, so x 50 to 878; nodes y 56 to 276). Disk zone: D3.panel {x: 40, y: 320, w: 856, h: 300, tone: 'grey', title: 'disk'}; newest segment row D3.recs(stage, {x: 54, y: 390, w: 156, h: 52, gap: 12, colGap: 12, cols: 5, recs: D3.MEM.flushed}) with tag 'newest segment' (green, x 54, y 450?) ; older segment row D3.recs {x: 54, y: 520, w: 156, h: 52, gap: 12, colGap: 12, cols: 4, recs: D3.MEM.old} with a grey tag 'older segment'. Write chips: D3.recCell chips (rec from D3.MEM.writes) fly in via t.set(i, {k, fly: {from: {x: 20, y: 150}, f}}). Query tag D3.tag {x: 40, y: 300?, text: 'get fig', tone: 'blue'} sits between zones at y 292 (small).

TIMELINE. 0.3-1.2 zones pop; the older segment row is already there. WRITES: write i (0-4) starts at 1.2 + 0.85 i: node i flies 0.6 s along its route (f 0 -> 1, from {x: 20, y: 150} via the root) and its edge draws on at arrival (t.edge(i, {k})). 5.3 the tree is full: tag 'full' (orange) pops. FLUSH 6.0-8.2: a blue ring sweeps the nodes in sorted order D3.MEM.walk (0.4 s each, ring on node walk[j]) and copies pop into the newest-segment row left to right at the same moments; 8.2 tree edges and nodes fade (o -> 0) and a single node 'date 15' (fresh memtable) pops at the tree root position. READ 10.3: 'get fig' tag pops; 10.6 a blue ring on the memory zone then a red cross (L5.cross) pops: miss; 11.4 the ring moves to the newest-segment row, fig 11 turns green solid and a green tick pops: hit; 12.5 the older segment's 'fig 8' stays grey (never read). Hold.

Copy the frame of videos/a6/scene-11-recap.js and videos/l5/scene-10-recap.js: kicker 'RECAP', headline 'Remember', Pebble via V.mascot('pebble', {size: 168, mood: 'love'}) at x 840, y 38, three v-card rows (x 72, tops 240 / 444 / 648, 936 x 180, appear 0.8 / 1.9 / 3.0) each with a 340 x 140 pictogram area at x 16, y 10 (zoom 1.1) and a bold two-line label at x 440 (36 px, at most 22 characters per line), then the blue call-to-action sticker 'Next: Workshop 3.W' at 6.8. EVERY PICTOGRAM PLAYS ONCE AND HOLDS ITS FINISHED FRAME (no loop, no reset); the video ends on a calm complete frame. Pictogram starts 0.4 s after their row appears. Numbers from D3 (D3.COST, D3.HASH, D3.MERGE) asserted.

helpers: FILES: videos/d3/common.js (pure data and algorithms, asserts on load), common-2.js (tags, chips, stats, discs, tokens, cards, labels, the database and memory icons, the movable pointer D3.ptr and the bracket D3.span, D3.seq / D3.along / D3.pop), common-3.js (D3.recs record lists with byte-offset gutters, D3.entries key -> number rows, D3.panel, D3.cell / D3.recCell), common-4.js (D3.mergeRig and D3.tree). Everything hangs off window.VID.d3; scenes start with const V = window.VID, D3 = V.d3, L5 = V.l5. videos/ds-3.html loads engine.js, cards.js, l5/common.js, then d3/common.js to common-4.js, the scenes, audio/ds-3.js. READ the long API comment at the top of every helper file first. DATA (common.js): D3.LOAD, D3.runLog / D3.LOG / D3.COST, D3.PLAYS / D3.hashIndex / D3.HASH, D3.segment / D3.compact / D3.SEG, D3.LIM, D3.mergeSegments / D3.MERGE, D3.sparseFind / D3.SPARSE, D3.buildTree / D3.readPath / D3.MEM, D3.size / D3.offsets / D3.hash, D3.same / D3.close (throw clear Errors), D3.rng. DRAWING: D3.tag/chip/stat/disc/token/card/label (set(state) every frame), D3.recs(parent, {x, y, w, h, cols | rows, recs, gutter, marks}) -> f.set(i, {tone, solid, ghost, tomb, key, val, text, k, x, y, s, o, ring, ringK, mark}), f.mid/left/right/top/bottom/slot/gutterMid(i); D3.entries -> m.set(i, {val, ring, valRing, bump, k}); D3.panel; D3.ptr (movable arrow, set({x1,y1,x2,y2,k})), D3.span (bracket), D3.disk / D3.ram icons; D3.mergeRig(...).update({p, k, o}) / info(p); D3.tree(...).set(i, {fly: {from, f}}) / edge(i, {k}). Tones: green red orange blue purple grey.
